It's a research institute.
Its kitchen is one third.
slides.subline: Onjium, 49 Hyoja-ro, Jongno-gu — a One MICHELIN Star dining room across from Gyeongbokgung's stone wall, ranked No. 14 on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 2026

slides.label: workshops in the institute — clothing, food and dwelling. Only one of them serves dinner.
slides.note: Onjium's official site describes itself as a traditional culture research institute, opened in 2013, running three workshops in Seochon: otgongbang (clothing), matgongbang (food) and jipgongbang (dwelling). The restaurant is the public face of the food workshop. Korean coverage traces the institute back to Arumjigi, a civic heritage group. Sources: onjium.org, MICHELIN Guide, Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, ELLE Decor Korea

items.d: The MICHELIN Guide's own entry keeps Onjium at One Star in the Seoul & Busan 2026 selection, and describes a team reinterpreting traditional Korean flavours through modern technique and years of research
Asia's 50 Best Restaurants ranked it No. 14 this year, after No. 10 in 2025. Its English Wikipedia entry records No. 21 in 2024

items.t: The menu comes out of old books
items.d: Both the guide and the 50 Best listing describe dishes rebuilt from centuries-old Korean recipe manuals. Korean reservation listings note the menu turns over roughly every two months

items.t: The name is a claim about method
items.d: Asia's 50 Best translates onjium as "creating in the right way." The institute's own site states its purpose as past and present meeting completely, in order to build the future

slides.title:
The restaurant is
the research, published.
slides.body:
Most fine dining rooms research in order to cook. Onjium's paperwork runs the other way.

It opened in 2013 as a traditional culture research institute in Seochon, with three workshops under one roof: one studying Korean dress, one studying Korean food, one studying Korean houses. Korean design press traces the dwelling workshop back to Arumjigi, a civic group set up to keep traditional culture in working use rather than in a museum case. The kitchen — matgongbang, the food workshop — is one third of that programme.

So the dining room is where one workshop's findings get served. Chefs Cho Eun-hee, a court cuisine specialist, and Park Sung-bae rebuild dishes out of centuries-old recipe manuals, and Korean booking listings note the menu rotating about every two months. Asia's 50 Best describes hanbok and scale models of hanok displayed on the building's other floors — the other two workshops' output, in the same building.

The non-obvious part: a restaurant this decorated is usually the institution. Here it is a department.

items.d: Seochon, directly across from the stone wall of Gyeongbokgung Palace. Asia's 50 Best lists the restaurant's phone as 02-6952-0024; the institute's food workshop line is 02-725-6610

Listings show lunch 12:00–15:00 and dinner 18:00–22:00, Tuesday through Friday, with Monday, Saturday and Sunday closed. A four-day week is unusual enough to be worth confirming before you plan around it
Korean booking platforms describe it as 100% reservation-only, with each Monday at 11:00 opening the slots five weeks ahead. That cadence matters more than walking distance here
Pairings are priced separately: wine at 120,000 won with lunch and 180,000 at dinner, traditional Korean liquor at 80,000 and 120,000. The dinner course price was not listed on the sources we checked

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal review.
Every fact here comes from published sources, checked in September 2026.
slides.by:
We have not eaten here. Whether a 200,000 won lunch is worth it to you is your call, not ours.
Prices, hours, menus and booking rules change without notice — confirm directly before you go.

caption:
A One MICHELIN Star dining room that is technically a department of a research institute.

Onjium sits across from Gyeongbokgung, in an institute with three workshops — clothing, food, dwelling. The restaurant is the food one, No. 14 in Asia this year.

We haven't eaten here, and a 200,000 won lunch is yours to judge.

Sources in the last slide.
